subject: botany_2
question_text: Why does Swiss cheese have big holes? Name the bacteria responsible for it.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.48, printed question 135. insider_note: Two facts: carbon dioxide, and Propionibacterium. Both are short, so write both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Why the holes
steps.margin_note: The gas and how it is trapped. Four lines.
lines: The large holes in Swiss cheese are caused by the
production of large amounts of CARBON DIOXIDE.
The gas is trapped in the setting cheese and
forms bubbles, which become the holes.
steps.why: The cheese sets while the bacteria are still producing gas, so the bubbles are trapped where they form.
common_mistakes: Saying the holes are made by air. They are made by CARBON DIOXIDE from the bacteria.
Saying the holes are cut into the cheese. They form as the cheese sets.

steps.label: The bacterium
steps.margin_note: The genus and the species if you know it, plus the flavour point.
lines: The bacteria used for cheese also give it its
steps.why: The same fermentation that makes the gas also makes the flavour compounds, which is why one bacterium is chosen for both.
common_mistakes: Naming Lactobacillus. Lactobacillus makes curd; PROPIONIBACTERIUM makes the Swiss cheese holes.
Naming no bacterium. Half the question is the name.
